item.title: Lake Haruna: A Crater Lake with Winter Ice Fishing — Guide
item.description: Lake Haruna sits within the caldera of Mount Haruna, its calm waters framed by the mountain’s distinctive jagged peaks, including the sharply pointed Sugenoyama, creating one of Gunma’s most photogenic natural landscapes. Warmer months bring pedal boats, lakeside walking paths and hiking trails up the surrounding peaks, while in the coldest winters, when the lake freezes solid, it transforms into a popular ice-fishing destination where visitors drill through the ice to catch smelt, a distinctive seasonal activity.

item.title: Lake Towada: Aomori's Crater Lake & Boat Tours — Guide
item.description: Lake Towada is a double volcanic crater lake of astonishing clarity, sitting 320 m above sea level on the Aomori–Akita border. The lakeside ‘Maidens’ statue, a 50-minute sightseeing cruise, and some of Japan’s finest mid-October foliage make it the natural climax of a Towada–Oirase trip. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Towada, Aomori (Akita border) Hours Lake open; cruises ~9:00–16:00 Admission Free; cruise ~¥1,500 Time needed 1.

item.title: Zao Okama Crater Lake: Yamagata's Emerald Volcano — Guide
item.description: Zao’s Okama crater lake is one of Japan’s most spectacular volcanic phenomena — an almost perfectly circular caldera filled with water of an otherworldly emerald-green colour caused by dissolved sulphur compounds. The Zao Echo Line toll road reaches the rim, making this one of Japan’s most accessible volcanic craters, with the colour shifting between deep teal and bright lime with the weather. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Zao, Yamagata (Miyagi border) Hours Echo Line ~Apr–Nov, daytime Admission Toll road fee applies Time needed About 1 hour Best time Summer–autumn; clear days for best colour What to See The near-perfectly circular emerald-green crater lake.
